label: Erythropygia_quadrivirgata
summary: The bearded scrub robin (Tychaedon quadrivirgata), also known as the eastern bearded scrub robin, is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in eastern and southern Africa. This species was formerly placed in the genus Cercotrichas.

appearance.description: Its length is 15–17 cm (5.9–6.7 in), and its weight is approximately 20–31 g (0.71–1.09 oz). The male and female are alike, with the female being slightly smaller. The crown and upperparts are mostly dark olive-brown.
appearance.colors: The crown and upperparts are mostly dark olive-brown. The tail is dark brown, with the outer feathers having white tips.
appearance.wings: The wing coverts are grey-brown with olive-brown edges.

juvenile.notes: The juvenile is paler brown, with black patterns on its crown and back, and its underparts are buff, with dark patterns.

behaviour: The bearded scrub robin is usually found in pairs or small groups. Its calls include chuck, chrrrt, chek-chek-kwezzzzzzz and seeeep. Its song is a series of melodious whistles and may mimic some other species of birds.

where_found.habitat: It is found in Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Somalia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe, with a distribution size estimated at 5,390,000 km2 (2,080,000 sq mi). It is mostly found at elevations of below about 1,000 m (3,300 ft).
